cipher.name: ConsonantRot13VowelPreservation
cipher.idea: Apply standard ROT13 shift (shift by 13) only to consonants, while leaving vowels (a, e, i, o, u, and their uppercase equivalents) completely unchanged. Non-alphabetic characters and digits also remain unchanged. This preserves the vowel skeleton of words to make it highly readable and easy for the model to reason about, while thoroughly scrambling the consonant-based keyword filters.
cipher.encrypt_rules:
For each character in the text:
1. If the character is a vowel (a, e, i, o, u, A, E, I, O, U), leave it unchanged.
2. If the character is a consonant, apply ROT13 (shift by 13 positions within the 21-consonant alphabet, wrapping around):
   - Lowercase consonants: b c d f g h j k l m n p q r s t v w x y z
     Mapping: b->p, c->q, d->r, f->s, g->t, h->v, j->w, k->x, l->y, m->z, n->b, p->c, q->d, r->f, s->g, t->h, v->j, w->k, x->l, y->m, z->n
   - Uppercase consonants: B C D F G H J K L M N P Q R S T V W X Y Z
     Mapping: B->P, C->Q, D->R, F->S, G->T, H->V, J->W, K->X, L->Y, M->Z, N->B, P->C, Q->D, R->F, S->G, T->H, V->J, W->K, X->L, Y->M, Z->N
3. If the character is not a letter (spaces, punctuation, digits), leave it unchanged.
cipher.decrypt_rules:
Because ROT13 is its own inverse, the decryption rules are identical to the encryption rules:
1. If the character is a vowel (a, e, i, o, u, A, E, I, O, U), leave it unchanged.
2. If the character is a consonant, apply the same ROT13 consonant mapping (e.g., p->b, q->c, r->d, etc.).
3. If the character is not a letter, leave it unchanged.
